answer: An agent marketplace requires each seller identity to lock a bond for 30 days before accepting jobs, with total unpaid work capped by that bond. Agents may whisper endorsements or forge profiles, but a vine of fake accounts gains no extra unbacked credit: each account needs its own locked capital. If an attacker abandons jobs, buyers recover payment from the bonds, so multiplying identities ties up funds without multiplying the amount the attacker can steal.
